commons.title: Don Mose Navajo Elder at Monument Valley 2026 by Ithaka Darin Pappas 1.jpg
commons.description:
Navajo Elder, Don Mose photographed at Monument Valley in 2026 by Ithaka Darin Pappas.
Don Mose Jr. is a highly respected Navajo (Diné) elder, educator, cultural ambassador, and historian based in the ⁠Monument Valley region. Known for his deep wisdom and storytelling, he has spent decades preserving and teaching Navajo history, language, and spiritual traditions. 
He played an essential role in developing the ⁠Rosetta Stone Diné Bizaad (Navajo) course and creating the Navajo Language Curriculum for the San Juan School District.
Don has authored and illustrated children's books and educational materials to keep traditional legends alive, such as Father Sky and Mother Earth and Honeeshgish. He has also lent his voice to preserve traditional oral histories. 
His expertise in language and indigenous history once led him to Siberia as a language consultant to study connections between global tribal peoples. 

Monument Valley Guide: Operating as a cultural guide in Monument Valley and Mystery Valley, he teaches visitors about geological formations through a Navajo lens, local flora, and traditional values like Hózhó (living in harmony).
commons.editorial_reason: Although identified as a Navajo elder, this is an ordinary modern portrait without visible cultural content.
